# Konspec UI

> Copy-paste HTML components for internal data applications. Light theme only. A component library written for the agent building your app.

You are reading the entry point for this design system. It is written for agents.
Read all of it before writing markup for a Konspec application, then fetch the
variants you need one at a time from /r/ and copy their markup verbatim.
registry.json is not one of them: it used to be the whole system in one
response and is now a short pointer at these endpoints. The Machine-readable
section at the end has each one and what it costs.

## Protocol

1. **Read llms.txt** — The stack, the tokens and the hard rules in one file, generated from the same source as this page. It is short. Read all of it.
   `GET /llms.txt`
2. **Fetch one variant at a time and copy verbatim** — The response body of a variant endpoint is the markup itself: no JSON envelope, no escaping, nothing to parse. Copy the string. Do not paraphrase markup you have already been handed, and do not reformat it into your own idiom. llms.txt lists every component with its variant ids, so once you have read it you can build these URLs yourself and never need an index. Fetch r/<id>.json when you need a component's rules, anatomy or accessibility notes rather than its markup: it carries no html at all, so it is a few thousand tokens rather than the tens of thousands it used to be, and it is also where the variant names live when an id alone does not tell you which one to take. Fetch r/index.json only if you arrived without reading llms.txt.
   `GET /r/<id>/<variant>.html  →  the markup, ready to paste`
3. **Fetch the smallest thing that answers the question** — Three sizes, and the gap between them is wide enough that taking the wrong one costs more than the answer is worth. A variant is the markup and nothing else, a thousand tokens or two, and it is the only one of the three you need in order to build a screen. r/<id>.json is the component with its markup taken out — the rules, the anatomy, the behaviour, the accessibility notes and the name of every variant — and you fetch it when you need to know why a component is shaped the way it is, or which of its variants to take. r/index.json is every component summarised in one file, and it is for an agent that arrived here without reading llms.txt. registry.json is none of these any more: it was the entire system in one response, several times a context window, and it now returns a short pointer at these endpoints instead. It had to stop being the whole file because an agent that fetched it got a truncated one, and a truncated registry is worse than none — the components above the cut look complete and the ones below it look absent, and nothing in the response says which is which.
   `GET /r/<id>.json  →  rules and variant names, no markup`
4. **Match the reference implementation** — A complete procurement dashboard built only from these components. When the docs and a real screen disagree about spacing or hierarchy, the screen wins.
   `GET /reference/`
5. **Ask rather than choose** — If a colour, size, pattern, component or layout is not defined here, it does not exist yet. Stop and flag it rather than filling the gap yourself: name what is missing and what it has to do, and let a person add it to the framework. Adding one is a decision for a person, not a default you pick because the page looked empty. An invented component is worse than a blocked screen, because it ships, gets copied, and never gets the accessibility work. This covers missing variants of components that do exist, not just missing components.
   `// no new tokens, components or layouts without a human`

## Stack

- **css**: Tailwind CSS v4 — utility classes only. No component CSS, no @apply, no custom colour tokens.
- **js**: Alpine.js 3 for local UI state, plus two official plugins — @alpinejs/collapse for animated panels and @alpinejs/focus for dialog focus traps. Both load before Alpine core. State lives on the component root, never in a global store.
- **server**: htmx for partial swaps. Alpine does not fetch.
- **charts**: Chart.js 4 via CDN, pinned, and only on pages that plot something. Colours are read out of the DOM at init, never written as hex: series from the HTML legend swatches, grid from the card border.
- **icons**: Lucide via CDN — <i data-lucide="name"></i>, hydrated by lucide.createIcons().
- **build**: None. Snippets are plain HTML and paste into Django, Flask or a static file unchanged.

## Rules

Every one of these exists because breaking it produced a visible defect at
least once. They are not style preferences.

1. **Use what is already here.** Before writing any markup, look for it in the component list in llms.txt. If a component or a page layout is already defined, copy its markup from /r/<id>/<variant>.html — writing your own version of something the registry defines is the defect this rule exists to prevent, because two implementations of one thing drift apart and only one of them ever gets the accessibility work. The layout entries are mandatory, not examples: a screen with a title and actions is page-header, a create-or-edit screen is form-page, and a queue worked one record at a time is list-detail. The shell that holds all of them is the next rule, and it is not optional. If what you need is not here, stop and flag it: name the thing, say what it has to do, and let a person add it to the framework. Do not invent a component, a layout or a pattern to fill the gap, and do not ship a one-off approximation of one under another name. A missing entry is a decision for a person; an invented one is a defect that ships and then gets copied. The same applies one level down, to variants: if the component is here but the variant you need is not, flag that too. Changing the labels, figures and records inside a variant is expected and is what copying it is for; reshaping one into a state, density or arrangement the registry does not list is a new variant, and a new variant is an addition to the framework rather than a local edit.
2. **Every signed-in screen is app-shell.** This is the one layout decision that is already made, and it is not a default you may weigh against alternatives. If a signed-in user can reach the page, the page is app-shell with the screen's own content inside <main>, copied from /r/app-shell/default.html like any other component. There are four exceptions and no more. Two are about context the shell cannot get: auth-page and error-page, because the shell reads the navigation, the counts and the signed-in user out of context that a signed-out visitor or a failed request may not have. Two are about a user the shell was not built for: portal-page, where the reader is an external supplier and the nav, the counts and the internal identity do not exist for them at all; and focus-page, the shop-floor screen where the chrome is not merely useless but harmful, because a rail takes target area away from a gloved hand and a nav link is a route to losing an uncommitted count. The test for the last two is narrow and you should expect to fail it: the shell has to be actively wrong for this reader, not merely unnecessary. A screen that simply feels cluttered is app-shell. Do not assemble a shell of your own out of sidebar and topbar. Those entries document the shell's parts and exist so its own variants can be built; a hand-rolled sidebar-plus-topbar is a second implementation of app-shell, and two implementations of one thing drift apart while only one of them keeps the accessibility work. Do not ship a lighter shell for one screen, and do not start a page at <main> because the screen looked simple enough not to need chrome. The shell owns the skip link, the nav landmark, the off-canvas focus trap, the collapse persistence, the command palette and the keyboard shortcuts; a page that skips it loses every one of them silently and still reviews as fine, because everything it dropped is invisible until somebody uses a keyboard or a phone. The test is the response, not the screen: if a signed-in request returns a page, it is app-shell unless it is one of the four named above. An htmx partial swapped into a shell already on screen is not a page and must not repeat it.
3. **Keep the data-kui attribute.** Every variant's root element carries data-kui="<component>/<variant>" — badge/table, app-shell/default. It is the only way to find, in an application nobody has touched for a year, which markup came from this framework and which entry it came from: grep data-kui across the repo and every pasted component answers for itself. Keep it on the element you copied it onto, keep the value exactly as the registry gives it, and do not add one by hand to markup that is not a copy of that variant — a wrong id is worse than none, because the next person updating that component will trust it. It is inert: no styling, no behaviour, no script reads it at runtime. Updating from it is something you do when a person asks for it and never on your own initiative: grep data-kui across the application, and for each hit fetch /r/<component>/<variant>.html, which is always the current markup for that entry, and diff it against the pasted copy. Nothing records which copies are stale, and nothing needs to — the diff is the answer. What you carry across is the class list and the structure. What you leave alone is everything the application put there: the labels, the template variables and tags, the hx-* attributes, the Alpine state and handlers, the ids and the form field names. A component is a shape, not content, so replacing a pasted block wholesale with the registry version silently deletes the work that made it a real screen. Where the two disagree on structure rather than on classes, stop and say so rather than reshaping the copy to match: the local version may have been changed deliberately, and that is a question for a person.
4. **Stock Tailwind only.** No custom CSS, no @theme colours, no arbitrary hex. Arbitrary values are for one-off sizes, never for colour.
5. **Light theme only.** There is no dark mode and none is planned. A second theme doubles the review surface for no benefit in an office tool.
6. **Never bind Alpine on a Lucide icon.** createIcons() replaces the <i> with an <svg>, destroying any :class on it. Bind on a wrapping span instead. The same class of bug bites one step further out: Alpine removes only the classes it added, so a class written into the markup on an element whose class is also bound survives every state change — a scroll-spy rail written that way marks two headings at once, forever. And a state class with no colour of its own, border-l-2 with no border-*, renders in currentColor until Alpine boots, which on a slow page is a dark rule down every item and on a page where Alpine fails is permanent. A marker element that is transparent at rest and carries no static class is the shape that cannot fail either way.
7. **Never add cursor-pointer.** Tailwind v4 preflight drops it from buttons. One base rule fixes every element; 300 utility classes do not.
8. **Colour means data state.** Red, amber and green describe what a record is doing. Never decoration, never a brand accent. They appear as a dot or an icon, never as a field of colour behind text.
9. **The accent is graphite.** zinc-700. Interactive text is zinc-900 plus an underline, not a colour.
10. **Alerts are neutral.** White card, zinc border, colour only in the icon. A full-width red field shouts louder than the overdue rows it describes.
11. **Focus is an outline, never a ring.** ring-* compiles to box-shadow, and forced-colours mode drops every box-shadow, so a ring is the one focus style guaranteed to vanish for the users who most need it. Write focus-visible:outline-3 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-zinc-700/15, and take the negative offset when the control sits flush inside a scroller that would clip it. outline-none is allowed only on a field whose wrapper draws the outline for it, because Tailwind resolves outline-style through a variable: outline-none on the same element kills its own focus outline while leaving the width and colour set, which measures as styled and renders as nothing.
12. **Every tinted shape carries its ring.** A tinted shape is bg-zinc-200 with ring-1 ring-inset ring-zinc-300 — pills, chips, avatars, icon wells, control tracks, the selected nav item, all of them. A tinted surface is bg-zinc-100 — the page, a selected row, the highlighted option in a menu — and a band recessed inside a white surface is bg-zinc-50, which is a table header or a zebra row. Give a shape the surface fill and it measures 1.00 contrast against the surface it sits on, which is not low contrast but the identical colour, and it disappears. One step of fill separates them and the ring holds the edge. Solid shapes need no ring, and it is ring rather than border so adding it reflows nothing. One exception, and only one: inline code inside a sentence takes the tint without the ring. A ring drawn around two words mid-paragraph cuts the line of the text it sits in, and the shape is already separated from the prose by the mono face.
13. **Hover never lands on the surface behind it.** A hover fill that equals the fill underneath it is not a subtle hover, it is no hover: the control loses its surface and the one thing the cursor is on reads as less present than the things it is not on. The page is bg-zinc-100, so a bordered white button sitting on the page cannot hover to zinc-100 — it dissolves and leaves its border behind. Two kinds of interactive thing, and the split is the same one the tinted-shape rule draws. A SHAPE is self-sized and rounded on every corner: a button, an icon button, a menu trigger, a chip. It hovers to the chip fill zinc-200 wherever it sits, because a shape has to read against whatever it is dropped onto — white if it rests white on a white card, and one step further to zinc-300 if it is already sitting on a zinc-200 track. A SURFACE is a full-bleed band: a table row, a menu item, a sidebar link, a member of a joined strip whose corners are shared with its wrapper. It steps once off the band it crosses, so zinc-100 inside a white panel and zinc-200 on the page. Anything with a solid fill of its own ignores all of this and steps one deeper: zinc-700 to zinc-800, red-600 to red-700, zinc-200 to zinc-300. node tools/build.js checks every variant against this and fails the build rather than warning, so the rule is not something anyone has to remember at the call site.
14. **A region may scroll sideways. The page may not.** Nothing in this system produces a horizontal scrollbar on the document at 390px — that is the rule the build cannot check and every review has to. What a wide thing does instead is scroll inside its own box: a comparison matrix, a rate grid, a board of stages, a printed line table. Three things come with that box and none of them is optional. It carries relative, because an sr-only span inside a scroller has no positioned ancestor otherwise, resolves against the document, escapes the clip and widens the whole page — this has now been the cause of a 390px overflow in four separate components and it is invisible in review because the element it comes from is invisible. It carries role="region", tabindex="0" and an accessible name, because Chromium will not give keyboard focus to an overflow container on its own and a matrix nobody can scroll without a mouse is a matrix half the users cannot read. And below the width at which it starts to clip it carries a line of text saying so, at text-[12px]/4 text-zinc-500 — there is no gradient, no fade and no arrow in this system, so the affordance is a sentence.
15. **Status colour lives in the dot.** Every status pill is the same graphite shape — bg-zinc-200, ring-zinc-300, zinc-700 text, the same fill an avatar takes. What separates Open from Overdue is a 6px dot. A column of tinted pills reads as a traffic light and stops meaning anything by the twelfth row; a column of identical pills with one red dot in it reads at a glance. This is the alert rule — colour only in the marker — applied to a pill.
16. **Paper is a medium, not a breakpoint.** Two entries print: document-page for A4 paperwork and label-sheet for die-cut label stock. What they established holds for anything else that ever does. Screen chrome carries print:hidden and the document is what is left. Backgrounds do not print, so nothing may carry meaning in a fill — which means a printed document has no status pill at all, because the 6px dot is a background circle and on paper the state has to become a word. A watermark is the same mistake twice. Structure comes from borders, and hierarchy from weight rather than from a darker grey: border-zinc-300 is about 16% grey on paper and a thermal printer, which is one bit deep, dithers it. Do not trust a breakpoint to mean paper — A4 portrait is 794 CSS px so md: applies and lg: does not, but the print dialog's Scale field changes the layout width, and at 50% every lg: rule switches on; where the printed shape must differ, write print:. Put break-inside-avoid on every row, on a totals block and on a signature block, because a total split across two sheets is a defect. Nothing inside a sheet is sticky: it prints on the first page and leaves a hole on the rest. Page numbers and carried-forward subtotals come from the view, because counter(page) in an @page margin box is not implemented in Chrome and no CSS can sum the previous sheet. And a barcode is an <img> whose src the server renders — not a font, which cannot do QR error correction, and not a JavaScript library, which draws after paint and is therefore not there when window.print() fires, so the sheet comes out blank exactly where every symbol should be. @page itself is an at-rule and can never be a Tailwind utility: it is the one piece of hand-written CSS this system needs, it goes in the project stylesheet beside the x-cloak rule, and because the last @page parsed wins for every printed page in the document, a deployment that prints both A4 paperwork and 100x50mm labels needs one print base per medium rather than one stylesheet for both.
17. **One shade per meaning.** Info is zinc-400, success emerald-600, warning amber-700, danger red-600 — and a warning is amber-700 in a component and amber-500 only when it is a dot, because a 1.5px stroke and a 6px disc need different weights of the same colour. Nothing takes a -50 tint or a -200 ring: a coloured icon well is still bg-zinc-200 with ring-zinc-300. Pick the shade from the token table, never by eye.
18. **Survive 390px.** Tables become stacked cards. Nothing scrolls sideways on a phone, with one exception: a carousel, where the sideways scroll is the component itself, and which snaps and peeks so it never looks like a layout that broke.
19. **No template x-for inside svg.** It is parsed in the SVG namespace and has no .content. Use divs, or a conic-gradient for donuts.
20. **x-cloak on anything hidden at first paint.** Alpine boots after the HTML renders. Without it, every dropdown flashes on load.
21. **Every text size carries its leading.** text-[13px] compiles to font-size alone — arbitrary sizes emit no line-height, so the element silently inherits whatever an ancestor left. Always write the slash form, text-[13px]/5. Sizes come from the seven steps; only prose may take a looser leading than the default pairing.
22. **Guard the Lucide re-hydration loop.** createIcons() leaves data-lucide on the <svg> it generates, so re-running it on every DOM mutation re-renders every icon forever. Guard on document.querySelector("[data-lucide]:not(svg)") or animations stutter while the DOM never settles.

## Tokens

Stock Tailwind. The class name is the token — there is no theme file to import.

### Surfaces

- **Page** `bg-zinc-100` — The scrolling page behind everything. Nothing inside a white surface may take this fill — same hex twice is a 1.00 contrast, and the card reads as a hole.
- **Surface** `bg-white` — Cards, panels, sidebar, topbar, table bodies.
- **Recessed** `bg-zinc-50` — A band inside a white surface: table header, zebra row. Lighter than the page, so it can never be read as the page showing through.
- **Edge** `border-zinc-300` — The outer edge of anything sitting on the page. White on zinc-100 is 1.10 and a zinc-200 edge is the first thing a washed-out panel drops.
- **Border** `border-zinc-200` — Edges inside a surface: inputs, a strip that ends a region, a nested panel.
- **Divider** `border-zinc-100` — Rows inside a card that is already bordered. On white only — on any tinted surface it computes to the surface.

### Text

- **Primary** `text-zinc-900` — Headings, values, anything you read first.
- **Secondary** `text-zinc-600` — Labels, descriptions, secondary copy.
- **Tertiary** `text-zinc-500` — Timestamps, hints, placeholder text.
- **On dark** `text-zinc-400` — The scale inverts on a zinc-900 band — the footer, the agent handoff. Darkening secondary text there makes it less readable, not more.

### Accent

- **Solid** `bg-zinc-700` — Primary buttons, progress fills, chart bars, the active nav marker.
- **Hover** `bg-zinc-800` — Hover state of anything accent-filled.
- **Tint** `bg-zinc-100` — A selected row, the highlighted option in a menu — surfaces, never shapes.
- **Chip** `bg-zinc-200` — Every tinted shape: badges, avatars, icon wells, control tracks, the selected nav item. One step deeper than the page so it keeps a fill of its own on either surface, and one deeper again for its ring.
- **Link** `text-zinc-900 underline underline-offset-2` — Interactive text. Colour is not the signal — the underline is.

### Semantic colour

One shade per meaning, and the same shade in every component. Pick from this
table rather than by eye. No -50 tints, no coloured rings — a coloured icon
well is still bg-zinc-200 with ring-zinc-300.

| tone | icon | mark you read | dot or bar | means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Info | `info` | `text-zinc-500` | — | Neutral notice. Grey, because nothing is wrong. |
| Success | `check-circle-2` | `text-emerald-600` | `bg-emerald-600` | Finished, posted, sent. Same green as the Closed dot. |
| Warning | `alert-triangle` | `text-amber-700` | `bg-amber-500` | Waiting, expiring, over a limit. 700 for marks you read — a 1.5px amber-500 stroke on white is illegible. |
| Danger | `alert-circle` | `text-red-600` | `bg-red-600` | Overdue, failed, destructive. Same red as the Overdue dot. |

### Typography

Inter and JetBrains Mono, self-hosted at assets/fonts.css. Nothing is fetched
from a font CDN at runtime.

Arbitrary font sizes compile to a font-size with no line-height, so every size
is written in the slash form and the pairing below is the default.

- `text-[11px]/4` — uppercase labels, counts, badge text
- `text-[12px]/4` — help text, timestamps, secondary lines
- `text-[13px]/5` — buttons, table cells, default component text
- `text-[14px]/5` — body copy, inputs, prose
- `text-[16px]/6` — card, dialog and panel titles
- `text-[20px]/7` — section headings, error page titles
- `text-[24px]/7` — page titles, KPI figures
- `text-[32px]/9` — the one value read at arm's length on a shop-floor screen — a scanned code, a counted quantity. focus-page only, and never more than one per screen

Three weights, and no others:

- `font-normal` (400) — body copy, table cells, anything you read as a sentence
- `font-medium` (500) — anything that labels or acts — buttons, table headers, alert titles, nav items
- `font-semibold` (600) — headings, KPI figures, panel titles

Two tracking values, plus the default:

- `tracking-wider` — 11px uppercase labels only
- `tracking-tight` — headings at 20px and above
- `normal` — everywhere else. No arbitrary em values.

### Shape

- rounded-lg controls; rounded-xl panels; rounded-full pills; 36–44px control height.
- Every number gets tabular-nums, without exception. Columns of figures that do not line up are a bug.

## Status colours

Fixed. Do not reinterpret per screen. Colour describes what the record is
doing; the accent is graphite precisely so these stay meaningful.

| status | pill | dot | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | `bg-zinc-200 text-zinc-600 ring-1 ring-inset ring-zinc-300` | `bg-zinc-400` | Not real yet — nothing has been submitted |
| Cancelled | `bg-zinc-200 text-zinc-600 ring-1 ring-inset ring-zinc-300` | `bg-zinc-400` | Ended without completing. Inert, like a draft — not emerald, because it is over but that is not good news |
| Open | `bg-zinc-200 text-zinc-700 ring-1 ring-inset ring-zinc-300` | `bg-zinc-500` | Live, and nothing is wrong with it |
| Pending | `bg-zinc-200 text-zinc-700 ring-1 ring-inset ring-zinc-300` | `bg-amber-500` | Awaiting somebody's decision — this is the word for an item sitting in an approval inbox |
| Approved | `bg-zinc-200 text-zinc-700 ring-1 ring-inset ring-zinc-300` | `bg-amber-500` | Approved, and now waiting on the vendor to deliver. It does NOT mean awaiting approval — that is Pending |
| On hold | `bg-zinc-200 text-zinc-700 ring-1 ring-inset ring-zinc-300` | `bg-amber-500` | Stopped on purpose, waiting on a person to release it |
| Overdue | `bg-zinc-200 text-zinc-700 ring-1 ring-inset ring-zinc-300` | `bg-red-600` | The alarm state — past its date, failed, or refused |
| Closed | `bg-zinc-200 text-zinc-700 ring-1 ring-inset ring-zinc-300` | `bg-emerald-600` | Finished, and finished well |

The five dots are meanings, not words. A state this table does not list takes the dot whose meaning matches, and never a new colour.

| dot | what it means |
|---|---|
| `bg-zinc-400` | Inert. Not real yet, or over without completing. Draft, Cancelled, Void, Superseded. |
| `bg-zinc-500` | Live and ordinary. Nothing is wrong and nobody is waiting. Open, In progress, Carried forward. |
| `bg-amber-500` | Waiting on somebody before it can move. Pending, Approved, On hold, Needs a reason, With finance. |
| `bg-red-600` | Stopped, failed or past its date. Overdue, Rejected, Blocked, Failed inspection, Short received. |
| `bg-emerald-600` | Finished and correct. Closed, Received in full, In tolerance, Passed. |

A verdict about a figure — In tolerance, Needs a reason, Blocked — is not a record state and does not belong in the table above, but it takes its dot from the same five meanings. Amber is a 6px disc at -500 and a 1.5px stroke at -700; that is the one place the same meaning takes two shades.

## Components

One line each, with the variant ids that entry has. The markup for one variant
is at /r/<id>/<variant>.html and the rules, anatomy and accessibility notes for
a component are at /r/<id>.json, which carries no markup and is a few thousand
tokens. Fetch those before building anything, rather than reconstructing a
component from the one-line description here: the description tells you which
one to fetch, not what it looks like. Where an id alone does not settle which
variant you want, /r/<id>.json names them all.

This list is a closed set, not a starting point. If what you are about to build
is on it, you must build it from the registry entry rather than from scratch.
That applies hardest to Layout: those entries are whole screens, and a screen
that is one of them is assembled from that entry, not redrawn.

If what you need is not on this list, it does not exist yet. Stop and flag it —
name the thing and what it has to do, and let a person add it to the framework.
Do not invent a component or a layout, and do not approximate one out of the
parts of another. Handing back a screen with a gap and a question is correct;
handing back a screen with an invented component in it is not.

Variants work the same way. Each entry below lists the variant ids it has, and
that list is closed too. Editing the labels, figures and records inside a
variant is expected. Reshaping one into a state, density or arrangement that is
not listed is a new variant, so flag it and let a person add it rather than
keeping it to yourself in one screen.

### Actions

- **Button** `button` — The standard action control. Exactly one primary button per view; everything else is secondary, ghost or a link. Variants: variants, sizes, icons, states, link, full-width, toolbar, destructive, confirm, toggle, async, unavailable, upload, django.
- **Button group** `button-group` — Several controls joined into one object. Two shapes only: a tinted track for choosing one of a set, and a bordered strip for actions that belong together — or, latched, for filters that can be on at once. Variants: segmented, attached, icon-toolbar, split, input, vertical, responsive, counts, toggle-group, sizes, disabled, stepper, row-actions, htmx, django.
- **Dropdown menu** `dropdown` — A menu of actions anchored to a trigger. Real focus walks the items one tabindex="-1" at a time; destructive items sit last, below a divider. Variants: default, row-actions, groups, checkbox-items, radio-items, shortcuts, submenu, destructive, account, split, descriptions, scrolling, context-menu, responsive, htmx.

### Forms

- **Label** `label` — The name of a control, bound to it with for and id or by wrapping it. The smallest component here, and the one that is most often drawn rather than connected. Variants: default, required, wrapping, legend, trailing, unit, help, hidden, states, invalid, horizontal, row, caption, htmx, django.
- **Field** `field` — Label, control, help text and error in one block. This is the unit every form is built from, and the thing that owns the wiring between the four. Variants: default, error, warning, required, horizontal, group, choice, dependent, action, grid, inline, readonly, server, django.
- **Input** `input` — Single-line text entry. The border lives on the wrapper, not on the control, so an icon, a unit or a clear button sits inside the focus outline instead of beside it. Variants: default, sizes, icon, amount, search, error, format, widths, password, disabled, inline, stale, htmx, django.
- **Input group** `input-group` — One text field — or a from and a to — and the things that qualify it: a unit, a currency, a scope select, an action, an answer the server fills in, all inside a single bordered enclosure that draws one focus outline for all of them. Variants: default, icon, button, select, range, stepper, action, search, textarea, error, locked, dense, responsive, htmx, django.
- **Select** `select` — One answer out of a short fixed list. A real <select>, styled through its wrapper the way an input is, and an Alpine listbox only for the rows an <option> cannot hold. Variants: default, groups, long, stale, states, multiple, filter, cell, rich, status, loading, cascade, autosave, django.
- **Textarea** `textarea` — Multi-line text entry. Same bordered wrapper as the input, a height measured in rows, and a counter when there is a limit worth showing. Variants: default, sizes, dense, counter, autogrow, toolbar, actions, template, error, disabled, copy, htmx, django.
- **Checkbox** `checkbox` — An independent on or off — one flag, a set of options, or the row selection a register's bulk actions run on. A real native box wearing accent-zinc-700. Variants: default, group, indeterminate, nested, cards, filters, dense, table, matrix, wide-matrix, wide-matrix-phone, states, locked, acknowledge, htmx, django.
- **Radio** `radio` — One of a set, and exactly one. Real native radios wearing accent-zinc-700, where the shared name is the group and the only way to mean none is an option that says so. Variants: default, descriptions, cards, inline, none, bands, conditional, table, rows, states, phone, htmx, django.
- **Toggle** `toggle` — A setting that takes effect the moment it is touched. A real checkbox carrying role="switch", with the track and the thumb beside it painted by peer-checked utilities. Variants: default, sizes, list, group, inline, states, table, dependent, readonly, confirm, htmx, refused, django.
- **Combobox** `combobox` — A text box that filters a list of records and commits one of them. The typing is a search; what reaches the server is a hidden input under it. Variants: default, multi, select-all, groups, rich, remote, create, states, selected-first, dense, filter, phone, htmx, django.
- **Attachment** `attachment` — The documents hanging off a record — a drop zone over the list of what is already there. Every file shows its type, size, who attached it and when. Variants: default, empty, uploading, failed, rejected, required, versions, readonly, single, compact, images, htmx, django.
- **Calendar** `calendar` — A month grid for picking a date or a range. Monday-first, tabular figures, and the same graphite selection the rest of the system uses. Variants: month, picker, range, jump, constrained, presets, marked, slot, period, locked, phone, native, htmx, django.
- **Questionnaire** `questionnaire` — A run of questions answered in order on one page — a QC checklist, a vendor assessment, a safety audit. One fieldset per question, the question text as its legend, and three equal tiles carrying the answer so a column of them can be read at a glance. Variants: question, run, observation, conditional, not-applicable, evidence, scale, multi, sheet, remaining, invalid, autosave, signed, django.

### Data display

- **Table** `table` — Rows of records with a sortable header. The workhorse of every register screen — order lists, GRN lists, ledgers. Variants: default, selection, row-actions, totals, grouped, linked-rows, long-values, dense, sticky-header, sticky-column, sticky-both, responsive, django.
- **Data table** `data-table` — The register screen assembled: a table with a search box, filters, sortable headers, column visibility, row selection, totals and a pager, all running off one array of records. Variants: default, compact, loading, paging, empty, filters, bulk, totals, expandable, export, server.
- **Pagination** `pagination` — Moves through a long register a page at a time, and says where you are in it. The range and the total are the component; the arrows are only what you do about them. Variants: simple, numbered, links, range, unknown-total, page-size, jump, dense, edges, keyboard, loading, failed, load-more, footer, django.
- **Stat card** `stat-card` — One number that matters, with the label above it and the change since the last period below. The tile a dashboard strip is made of, and the answer whenever the data is a single current value rather than a shape. Variants: default, delta, sparkline, grid, status, target, dense, period, filter, loading, stale, failed, empty, dashboard.
- **Chart** `chart` — Chart.js on a canvas, wearing this system's colours. The legend is HTML and doubles as the palette the canvas paints from, so a swatch and the line it names cannot drift apart. Variants: setup, line, bar, horizontal, stacked, donut, sparkline, table, toggle, period, responsive, empty, loading, failed, django.
- **Progress** `progress` — The determinate wait. A graphite rail filled to the fraction of a known total that is done — receipt against an order, lines closed on a GRN, quantity built against a plan — with the two figures written out beside it. Variants: bar, bare, steps, stage-failed, inline, tones, stalled, elapsed, stacked, radial, indeterminate, production, htmx, django.
- **Empty state** `empty-state` — What a region shows when it has nothing to draw. Several situations wearing one shape — nothing created yet, nothing matching the query, nothing asked for yet, nothing left to do, nothing this account may see and nothing that loaded — and the whole job of the component is saying which one it is. Variants: nothing-yet, no-results, too-short, filtered, archived, prerequisite, all-clear, error, permission, in-table, compact, inline-create, register, django.
- **Skeleton** `skeleton` — Grey blocks standing in the exact box the content will occupy — same rows, same leading, same column widths — so the first paint of a screen whose layout is already known lands without moving. Variants: text, heading, table, dense, cell, card, stats, list, form, chart, record, append, delayed, states, django.
- **Marker** `marker` — The mark that opens a list item — a dot, a number, an icon or a tinted well — drawn as a real element in a box the height of one line, so it holds its place when the item wraps. Variants: prose, dot, numbered, clauses, checklist, timeline, pending, register, rows, grouped, nested, steps, dense, django.
- **Spinner** `spinner` — The indeterminate wait. A graphite ring that turns while work of unknown length is in flight, and a line of text that says what the work is. Variants: default, sizes, label, motion, panel, inline, slot, queue, overlay, delayed, phases, states, stalled, django.

### Feedback

- **Alert** `alert` — An inline notice about the page or the record in front of the user. White card, zinc border, and the only colour is the icon. Variants: tags, compact, dismissible, remembered, action, confirm, responsive, records, overflow, progress, banner, form-errors, htmx, django.
- **Toast** `toast` — A short confirmation that an action the user just took has finished, pushed into a live region pinned to the bottom-left and gone a few seconds later. It reports an outcome; it is never where the outcome is recorded. Variants: default, tones, undo, held, link, error, stack, bulk, pending, retry, dismiss-all, posting, phone, htmx, django.
- **Alert dialog** `alert-dialog` — A dialog that interrupts to ask one question the user has to answer before anything else happens. Unlike a plain dialog it does not dismiss on a backdrop click, and unlike an in-place confirm it has room for the reason. Variants: confirm, destructive, typed, reason, consequences, bulk, blocked, running, refused, unsaved, django.
- **Dialog** `dialog` — A centred, dismissible panel over a dimmed page. Use it to take a handful of fields without leaving the list. Variants: form, scrolling, reference, submitting, errors, deferred, steps, stacked, wide, phone.
- **Sheet** `sheet` — A panel that slides in from the right edge, full height and a fixed width, over a list that stays visible behind it. Where one row of a register is read, amended, or walked one record to the next without giving up your place in the list. Variants: record, filters, loading, failed, form, unsaved, walk, stacked, phone, htmx.
- **Drawer** `drawer` — A panel flush to a horizontal edge of the viewport, sized to its content and capped short of the screen. The phone-shaped place to put a short action list, a quick filter, one record being edited, or the tray a multi-select fills. Variants: actions, filter, long, loading, error, edit, guarded, top, persistent, phone, django.
- **Badge** `badge` — A small pill that labels a record — status, tag or count. Every pill is the same graphite shape; a 6px dot carries the colour. Variants: status, inline, unknown, axes, sizes, icon, filter, removable, overflow, count, table, header, htmx, django.
- **Tooltip** `tooltip` — A short dark bubble that names the control under the pointer or under the keyboard. It carries a label and nothing else — no controls, no facts that are not already somewhere the user can reach without hovering. Variants: icon, placement, edge, truncated, inline, shortcut, disabled, table, arrow, scrolling, delay-group, rail, touch, row-actions.
- **Hovercard** `hovercard` — A card of record detail that opens under a link on hover or focus, after a deliberate delay, and stays open long enough to be read and clicked. Variants: default, vendor, user, item, long, placement, trail, htmx, cached, loading, error, restricted, mobile, django.
- **Popover** `popover` — A panel of controls anchored to a button and opened by a click. It holds things you focus and operate — a filter, a column list, a date range, a two-field edit — and the page behind it keeps working. Variants: default, filter, columns, column-filter, date-range, inline-edit, read-only, unsaved, saving, arrow, placement, responsive, htmx, django.
- **Avatar** `avatar` — Initials in a circle standing in for a person. Nothing in this system uploads a photograph, so a zinc tint and two letters is the component; where the identity provider hands one over, the photograph is a layer painted on top of the letters. Variants: sizes, self, photo, derived, org, with-name, stacked, count, in-row, presence, menu, placeholder, django.

### Navigation

- **Tabs** `tabs` — Switches between views of the same record without leaving the page. The panel below changes; the row above is a widget, not a menu, and the keyboard has to know the difference. Variants: underline, pill, card, scrollable, select, vertical, pinned, url, lazy, retry, states, guard, django.
- **Breadcrumbs** `breadcrumbs` — The path from the section root down to the record on screen. The last crumb says where you are and is not a link. Variants: default, record, truncated, overflow, loading, restricted, ambiguous, responsive, page-header, sequence, back, htmx, django.
- **Menubar** `menubar` — A row of menus across the top of a document — File, Edit, View — sharing one tab stop and one keyboard model. A desktop-application affordance, and most internal screens should not have one. Variants: default, shortcuts, checks, submenu, states, readonly, selection, confirm, dense, sticky, collapsed, trailing, htmx, django.
- **Navigation menu** `navigation-menu` — A horizontal bar of links to places, some of which open a panel of more links. Every item is an anchor, so the browser's own navigation gestures keep working, and aria-current says which one you are on. Variants: links, panel, columns, featured, icons, mixed, current, deep, restricted, scoped, edge, phone, htmx, django.
- **Sidebar** `sidebar` — The primary navigation panel of the console: a header, grouped menus with counts and submenus, and a footer for the signed-in user. It has three forms — a 256px panel, a 68px icon rail, and an off-canvas sheet over the page. Variants: default, counts, counts-async, nested, record, filter, permissions, rail, flyout, collapse, mobile, blocks, skeleton, django.
- **Topbar** `topbar` — The application header above the page content: the sidebar trigger, the context you are working in, what you can search and who you are signed in as. A real <header> holding a named <nav>, sticky over the column and out of the way of everything that opens above it. Variants: default, search, account, unread, toggle, context, impersonation, session, compact, crowded, sticky, phone, assembled, django.
- **Accordion** `accordion` — Sections of content that collapse to their heading. The heading is a button that toggles the panel below it. Variants: default, single, cards, summary, expand-all, form, states, phone, htmx, django.
- **Collapsible** `collapsible` — One trigger and one panel. The standalone disclosure — show more, an advanced section at the foot of a form, a filter bar that folds away. Variants: default, advanced, filters, native, card, controlled, states, tail, row, errors, findable, htmx, django.
- **Command palette** `command-palette` — A ⌘K overlay for jumping to a record or firing an action by typing. It is a shortcut over the navigation, never the only route to something. Variants: default, recents, kinds, unavailable, no-results, argument, prefix, phone, htmx, django.

### Layout

- **Container** `container` — The measurements every screen in this library is already making: how wide a page is, how far its content sits from the edge of the column, the three vertical spacings, the responsive column grid, and the rules for what may scroll and in which direction. A reference for the box the other layouts sit in, not a screen of its own. Variants: page, narrow, wide, stack, grid, regions, sticky, overflow, phone.
- **App shell** `app-shell` — The page skeleton: an icon rail that expands to a labelled sidebar, a topbar carrying the hamburger, breadcrumb, command palette and account menu, and a single scrolling main column. Everything else in the app renders inside the main column. Variants: default.
- **Page header** `page-header` — The top block of a page: where it sits in the app, what it is, what state it is in, and what you can do to it. One h1 per page and it lives here. Variants: default, trail, record, tabs, filters, back, sticky, overflow.
- **Card** `card` — A bordered white panel that groups one thing. A header names it, the body holds the content, and an optional footer carries totals or actions. Variants: default, actions, stats, section, table, clickable, grid, empty, django.
- **Separator** `separator` — The rule that divides content. Almost always a border on the thing beside it rather than an element of its own, and almost always silent to a screen reader. Variants: default, rows, vertical, labelled, menu, django.
- **Carousel** `carousel` — A horizontal rail of items that snaps one item at a time. CSS scroll snap does the moving; the arrows and the counter are the only JavaScript. Variants: default, peek, dots, photo, thumbnails, stats, empty, django.
- **List and detail** `list-detail` — A queue on the left and the record being worked on beside it. Arrow keys walk the list, Enter opens the record into the detail pane, and only the two panes scroll — the page behind them does not move. Variants: default, nothing-selected, responsive, search, three-pane, loading, qc-hold.
- **Form page** `form-page` — The layout a create or edit screen uses: one h1, the fields grouped in cards, a validation summary that links to every field that failed, and Save and Cancel where the user can always reach them. Variants: two-column, side-rail, sections, invalid, sticky-actions, line-items, wizard, readonly.
- **Auth page** `auth-page` — The signed-out screen: one centred card, the fewest fields that will do, and nothing else on the page. Sign in, the second factor after it, and every screen the user lands on when one of the two fails. Variants: signin, failed, forgot, sent, reset, otp, sso, locked.
- **Error page** `error-page` — The whole screen the user gets when the page could not be produced at all. It says what failed in their own terms, whether anything they did was saved, and gives one way back into an application whose navigation is not on this page. Variants: 404, 403, 500, maintenance, offline, expired, django.
- **Dashboard** `dashboard` — The screen a user lands on after signing in: a strip of figures, one plot, and the queues that are actually waiting for them. Every part of it already exists — this entry is the composition and the rules that govern it. Variants: default, queues, alerts, period, regions, role, empty, phone, django.
- **Index page** `index-page` — The register screen as a whole page: the breadcrumb and the one h1, the saved views, the filter band, the toolbar that becomes a selection toolbar, the table, the pager, and the states the page as a whole can be in. Variants: default, saved-views, filters, tabs, bulk, dense, empty, loading, django.
- **Record page** `record-page` — The screen for one record: the band that identifies it and says what state it is in, a strip of the figures that matter, and the sections of detail below it — line items, approvals, documents, activity — carrying only the actions the record's current state allows. Variants: default, rail, tabs, approvals, activity, states, permissions, phone, django.
- **Approval inbox** `inbox-page` — The screen an approver lives in: everything waiting on their signature in one queue, the record beside it, and the decision on a rail where the hand already is. Deciding removes the record from the queue and lands the user on the next one without a reload. Variants: default, advance, reject, pending, bulk, limits, delegated, empty, phone, django.
- **Board** `board` — Records in columns by the stage they are at, where each column is one stage and moving a card between two of them is a state change on the server. The column header carries the count, and every move can be made from the keyboard. Variants: default, card, totals, wip, pending, drag, empty, filters, phone, django.
- **Schedule page** `schedule-page` — What is planned and when, drawn with time as the axis: promised deliveries across a month, production against each line, a shift roster. Position carries meaning — further right is later, and a block twice as wide takes twice as long. Variants: month, week, resource, day, block, conflict, empty, filters, phone, django.
- **Compare page** `compare-page` — Several vendors' quotations against one enquiry, side by side, so a buyer can award the order. Line items down, vendors across, rates in the cells and the totals along the bottom — the comparative statement that is attached to the requisition and shown to whoever signs it. Variants: default, sticky, lowest, landed, terms, partial, award, phone, django.
- **Reconcile page** `reconcile-page` — Two sets of records that ought to agree, with the difference between them written out as a figure and the controls that make them agree — pairing, explaining and posting. The variance is the content; the rows that already agree are a count. Variants: three-way, tolerance, unmatched, match, partial, ledger, phone, post, clean, django.
- **Import page** `import-page` — The screen that takes a spreadsheet into the system: the file and the rules stated before it is picked, the column mapping, the review of what the system understood, the failures grouped by kind, and the write itself with a report at the end. Variants: upload, mapping, preview, errors, fix, committing, result, phone, django.
- **Search page** `search-page` — The whole-page answer to a query typed into the global search: the query echoed as the one h1, the results grouped by record type with a count on every group, the facets that narrow them, and the states the page is in when there is nothing to show yet or nothing to show at all. Variants: results, exact, facets, scoped, empty, loading, recent, syntax, phone, django.
- **Focus page** `focus-page` — One task on the whole screen with the application chrome removed: a bag scanned into a GRN at the gate, a bin counted at a rack, a sample passed or failed at the QC bench. Large targets, type one step up, and a scan field that never gives up the keyboard. Variants: scan, unknown, confirm, count, inspect, progress, offline, exit, django.
- **Settings page** `settings-page` — The configuration screen: a permanent nav of sections down one side and the section being changed beside it. One h1 for the whole screen, an h2 per section, and a Save that belongs to the section rather than to the page. Variants: default, dirty, immediate, grouped, series, roles, danger, phone, django.
- **Onboarding page** `onboarding-page` — The screen that tracks a deployment being configured: every task that has to be finished before a document can be raised, grouped, with what is done, what is blocked and on what, who owns each one, and what the page becomes once it is finished. Variants: checklist, task, blocked, resume, assigned, optional, complete, phone, django.
- **Audit page** `audit-page` — The whole system's audit trail as a page: who changed what, when, and what the value was before. Queried across records, actors, fields and dates, grouped by day, newest first, and append-only — nothing on this screen edits anything. Variants: default, diff, events, filters, record, more, export, empty, phone, django.
- **Docs page** `docs-page` — The manual inside the application: the standard operating procedures, the approval limits, the definitions a screen assumes you already know. The only screen in this library that is mostly prose, so the measure, the heading rhythm and what a link looks like inside a sentence are the component. Variants: article, prose, procedure, controlled, callouts, nav, search, phone, print, django.
- **Document page** `document-page` — The record as a sheet of paper: a purchase order, a GST tax invoice, a delivery challan, a goods receipt note. Laid out on A4, printed from the browser, and built so that what comes out of the printer is the same document that was on screen. Variants: purchase-order, invoice, challan, grn, draft, copies, multi-page, preview, django.
- **Label sheet** `label-sheet` — Labels that come off a printer and get stuck onto things: a bin label on a rack, a batch label on a drum, a pallet tag, a QC hold sticker. Either a grid of them on an A4 sheet of die-cut stock or one at a time on a continuous roll, sized in millimetres because the stock in the printer is. Variants: sheet, roll, sizes, content, start-position, align, preview, phone, django.
- **Portal page** `portal-page` — The screens a supplier signs in to: the orders you have placed with them, the acknowledgement, an invoice against a receipt, what has been paid, and their own details. One vendor is the whole application, and the layout is built to make that visible. Variants: shell, orders, acknowledge, upload, payments, profile, restricted, phone, django.

## Machine-readable

Cost is why this is split, so the cost is on the label. Fetch the smallest
thing that answers the question.

| endpoint | size | cost | what it is |
|---|---|--:|---|
| [r/index.json](r/index.json) | 136 KB | ~39k tokens | The spec and every component summarised, with variant ids. No markup. The largest thing you are ever asked to fetch whole. |
| `r/<id>.json` | median 16 KB, largest 27 KB (`sidebar`) | ~5k tokens / ~8k tokens | One component: rules, anatomy, behaviour, accessibility, and the id and name of every variant. No markup. |
| `r/<id>/<variant>.html` | median 6 KB, largest 45 KB (`app-shell/default`) | ~2k tokens / ~13k tokens | The markup, raw. No JSON envelope, no escaping, paste as-is. |
| `r/<id>.full.json` | median 91 KB, largest 189 KB (`search-page`) | ~26k tokens / ~54k tokens | The component and every variant's html in one file — what `r/<id>.json` used to be. Back-compat; you want the two rows above. |
| [registry.json](registry.json) | 1 KB | ~406 tokens | A pointer at this table. It was 7.2 MB, about 11× a 200k context window, and every agent that fetched it got a silently truncated file. |

The component list above prints every variant id, so once you have read this
file you can build a variant URL yourself and skip r/index.json entirely:
`GET /r/button/variants.html` returns the markup for button/variants and nothing
else. That is the common path — one read of llms.txt, then a few small ones.

Read the ids; do not guess them. Only 40 of the 74 components have a variant
called `default`, and 34 do not, so a guessed URL is a 404 rather
than a fallback. The ids are listed above precisely because they are not
predictable from the component name.
